ruling_text:
Case Number:
24TRCV00993
Hearing Date:

March 18, 2026
Dept:

B
Moving Party:

Hilbert Haghnazarzadeh
Responding Party:

Angel Ann Brown
Motion to Consolidate
The court considered the
moving, opposition, and reply papers.

RULING
The motion is GRANTED.

BACKGROUND
On March 21, 2024, plaintiffs Angel
Ann Brown and Jimmy Lee Brown filed a complaint against defendant Hilbert
Haghnazarzadeh.

On June 14, 2024, plaintiffs filed the first amended complaint against
defendant for (1) negligence, and (2) breach of implied warranty.
Plaintiffs allege that they are
tenants of defendant at a structure located at 12812-12816 Van Ness, Gardena CA
90249. Plaintiffs claim that the property suffered from habitability problems,
including rat and roach infestation, and sewage backups. Plaintiffs allege that
they asked defendant for repairs, and instead, defendant tried to force
plaintiffs from the property by shutting off their utilities.
Plaintiffs also allege that in or around February 2023, plaintiff Angel
Brown suffered a serious injury in the property’s flooded bathroom when she
slipped and fell headfirst. She alleges she lost several teeth and was knocked
unconscious.

On January 30, 2026, the Court found this action related with
25TRCV02272. In case 25TRCV02272, the same plaintiffs, in
pro per
, filed
a first amended complaint against defendant, erroneously sued as Rouhi
Haghnazarzadeh, for (1) illegal lockout, (2) constructive eviction, (3)
intentional infliction of emotional distress, (4) fraud &
misrepresentation, (5) retaliation – Civil Code section 1942.5, (6) defamation,
and (7) abuse of process.

In 25TRCV02272, plaintiffs allege they were tenants of the premises
located at 12812 Van Ness Ave. Gardena, CA. Plaintiffs allege that defendant
repeatedly engaged in illegal self-help evictions, lockouts, utility shutoffs,
forced entries, threats, retaliation, defamatory statements, and misuse of the
judicial process.

LEGAL AUTHORITY
“When actions involving a common
question of law or fact are pending before the court, it may order a joint
hearing or trial of any or all the matters in issue in the actions; it may
order all the actions consolidated and it may make such orders concerning
proceedings therein as may tend to avoid unnecessary costs or delay.”
(Code Civ. Proc. § 1048, subd. (a).)  The purpose of consolidation is
to enhance trial court efficiency by avoiding unnecessary duplication of
evidence and the danger of inconsistent adjudications.  (
See
Todd-Stenberg v. Dalkon Shield Claimants Trust
(1996) 48
Cal.App.4th 976, 978-979.)
Consolidation, however, is not
a matter of right; it rests solely within the sound discretion of the trial
judge. (
Fisher v. Nash Bldg. Co.
'(1952) 113 Cal.App.2d 397, 402.)'
Actions may be thoroughly “related” in the sense of having common questions of
law or fact, and still not be “consolidated,” if the trial court, in the sound
exercise of its discretion, chooses not to do so.' (
Askew v. Askew
'(1994)
22 Cal.App.4th 942, 964.)' It is not an abuse of discretion to deny a motion
for consolidation of actions where parties in each action are different or
issues are different.' (See'
Muller v. Robinson
'(1959) 174 Cal App 2d
511, 515.)' On the other hand, actions may be consolidated in the discretion of
the trial court whenever it can be done without prejudice to a substantial
right.' (
Carpenson'v.'Najarian
'(1967) 254 Cal.App.2d 856, 862.)'

DISCUSSION
Defendant moves for a court order consolidating this
action with
25TRCV02272
for all purposes.

Defendant
contends common issues of law and fact exist in both actions because these
actions involve alleged damages from the same events, same property, and same
parties.

Further, defendant argues he is being defended under the same
claim number for insurance purposes. Defendant argues consolidation of the
actions will promote substantial trial convenience and economy by avoiding
presentation of duplicative issues. Defendant argues he anticipates relying on
at least one defense which concerns the same legal question: whether plaintiffs
have a valid residential lease. Separate trials on this question could result
in inconsistent findings.

In plaintiffs’
untimely opposition,
plaintiffs argue that
although
both actions arise out of a landlord–tenant relationship involving the same
property, the claims asserted in each case involve materially different
operative facts, distinct legal theories, and separate categories of damages.
In the alternative, plaintiffs request that the Court consider less drastic
case management measures such as coordinated discovery or scheduling orders
rather than full consolidation for all purposes.
The Court finds that the cases should
be consolidated.

The cases involve the
same parties, same property, and stem from common facts.
It would promote judicial economy to have the
cases tried together.

ORDER
The
motion is GRANTED.

Moving
party is ordered to give notice.
